name: Scallop Lend
rootCause: A deprecated side contract (V2 rewards contract) tied to Scallop’s sSUI Spool rewards pool was exploited. The attacker exploited a missing validation in the reward accumulator logic (uninitialized variable in update_points function). By staking a small amount (0.2 SUI), they generated massive fake reward points (162 trillion), draining the entire leftover rewards pool of approximately 150,000 SUI. Core lending markets, user deposits, and active pools were unaffected. The team promptly froze the affected contract, committed to covering 100% of the loss from treasury, and resumed normal operations.

descriptions.text: A deprecated side contract (V2 rewards contract) tied to Scallop’s sSUI Spool rewards pool was exploited. The attacker exploited a missing validation in the reward accumulator logic (uninitialized variable in update_points function). By staking a small amount (0.2 SUI), they generated massive fake reward points (162 trillion), draining the entire leftover rewards pool of approximately 150,000 SUI. Core lending markets, user deposits, and active pools were unaffected. The team promptly froze the affected contract, committed to covering 100% of the loss from treasury, and resumed normal operations.

Scallop Lend was exploited on Sui on 26 April 2026, losing approximately $142,000 due to a reward logic bug in a deprecated auxiliary contract. The attacker manipulated a missing validation in the reward accumulator, allowing extraction of the full reward pool. Response actions contained further losses and protected user funds. A missing validation check in the deprecated sSUI Spool contract allowed the attacker to pair unrelated reward pools and accounts, fabricating trillions of reward points and draining the rewards pool in a single transaction.
